findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as a separate Git argument
findings.body: When `branch` contains caller-controlled text, interpolating it into `exec()` allows shell metacharacters and command substitutions such as `$(...)` to execute before Git runs. Preserve argv separation with `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` or otherwise avoid invoking a shell.

findings.title: [P2] Return the Git process so cancellation stops the operation
findings.body:
`exec()` returns the intermediate shell process rather than `git`. On Windows, calling `.kill()` while a long-running `git show` is active terminates `cmd.exe` but can leave Git running and holding the inherited output pipes, so cancellation does not end the work and completion can be delayed. The previous `execFile()` process represented Git directly.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Avoid interpolating branch names into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell, so a caller-controlled branch such as `main; touch /tmp/pwned` executes the appended command with the process’s privileges. The previous `execFile` implementation passed the branch directly to Git without shell interpretation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch argument out of a shell
findings.body:
`exec()` invokes a shell, and the interpolated `branch` value is not escaped. A branch argument such as `main; attacker-command` executes arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges. The previous `execFile()` implementation passed the value directly to Git without shell interpretation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Avoid spawning an extra shell for every branch lookup
findings.body:
`exec()` starts a shell before Git, adding another process and shell parsing/startup cost to every call. Repeated or concurrent branch lookups therefore consume roughly twice the process slots and additional memory compared with the previous direct `execFile()` invocation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation ownership of the Git process
findings.body:
The returned `ChildProcess` now represents the shell rather than Git. On platforms where the shell launches Git as a child, calling `.kill()` terminates only the shell and can leave a slow or blocked `git show` running and consuming CPU, network, and pipe resources. The prior direct invocation allowed cancellation to target Git itself.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
